olivia: CI turned red for PR #4129 — only `e2e/browser` job failed (timeout in puppeteer). Is there a quick way to rerun that axis without rebuilding images?
ci-bot: PR #4129 — workflow `ci/pipeline` run 12345 failed: `e2e/browser` (exit 1). Artifact: /artifacts/12345/e2e/video.mp4. Logs show `TimeoutError: Navigation timeout of 30000 ms exceeded`.
jake: You can do a job-level rerun with preserve-image to avoid full rebuild:```bash
cictl rerun --run 12345 --jobs e2e/browser --preserve-image
```That will re-execute only that job and keep the image/cache.
maria: If you suspect flake, add a small repeat to reduce noise:```bash
cictl rerun --run 12345 --jobs e2e/browser --preserve-image --repeat 3
```Also `--preserve-image` keeps docker layers and wheel caches.
sam: quick q — does `--preserve-image` also keep test fixtures/artifacts from previous steps (like KV caches)?
maria: `--preserve-image` keeps the built container. For in-run caches (test caches, kv), add `--keep-cache`. If you actually need a fresh compile but want to skip unrelated stages, use `--rebuild-only e2e/browser` (this rebuilds image for that job only).
rachel: Another option: in GH UI you can rerun a single job from the run page (3-dot menu) — that mirrors `cictl` behavior. For matrix jobs you can pick an axis there. If it's environment-related, check screenshots/video first.
jake: Quick triage checklist: 1) inspect video/screenshot and the failing test trace, 2) try local repro (`yarn test:e2e --grep "login flow" --headless`), 3) rerun single job with `--preserve-image`, 4) if it fails repeatedly, file a bisect and mark `flaky/test` and request oncall to bisect.
olivia: thanks — kicking off `--preserve-image` rerun now. will post results. :thumbsup:
